items: Contract Vulnerabilities: Review your current contract template today and locate every section covering project scope definition, payment milestones, and late payment terms.
Contract Vulnerabilities: Add a scope definition clause that explicitly lists deliverables and requires written change orders with agreed pricing before any additional work begins.
Contract Vulnerabilities: Define payment milestones that link specific deliverables to specific payment amounts and due dates so clients cannot hide behind vague completion language.
Contract Vulnerabilities: Include late fee language with both a trigger date and a consequence, such as your right to pause work when payment is 30 days overdue.
Payment Structure: Implement a deposit requirement for all new clients, typically 30-50% of the total project cost, to reduce financial exposure from the start.
Payment Structure: Break large projects into distinct phases where each phase completion triggers a specific payment amount rather than one lump sum at the end.
Payment Structure: Set explicit payment due dates tied to milestone approvals, such as requiring payment within 5 business days of written client sign-off.
Payment Structure: Establish your right to stop all active work immediately if a client fails to pay an overdue milestone, preventing additional unpaid labor.
Documentation Practices: Create written confirmation for every scope discussion using email or project management tools that generate timestamps and records.
Documentation Practices: Send formal delivery confirmations that require client acknowledgment, preventing the "I never received that" defense in future disputes.
Documentation Practices: Maintain organized records of all sent invoices, payment confirmations, client responses, and delivery receipts in a dedicated folder or system.
Documentation Practices: Document every client interaction about payment terms in writing rather than relying on verbal agreements that become impossible to verify later.
